This ducted ASHP is sized according to the load calculations in ACCA Manual J (Air Conditioning Contractors of America 2016) and system selection in ACCA Manual S (Air Conditioning Contractors of America 2014). ACCA Manual J provides the procedure for calculating the design heating and cooling loads of the building, while ACCA Manual S guides the selection of residential HVAC systems size. ACCA Manual S directs that ASHPs be sized to the dwelling's calculated cooling load with allowable oversizing limits. Oversizing limits are recommended, especially for single-stage equipment, because an ASHP sized to the heating load could be considerably larger than what the cooling load requires. This large difference in required size can lead to indoor humidity problems in some climate zones because short cycling reduces the ASHP's ability to dehumidify the space. ACCA Manual S seeks to avoid humidity-related comfort problems with its guidance on oversizing. These oversizing limits depend on the climate of the dwelling and the type of compressor. The oversizing limits for single-stage (reflective of this measure's compressor), two-stage, and variable-speed ASHPs are 15%, 20%, and 30%, respectively, and are implemented only for dwellings with mild winters or humid climates. data.content:
The system switches from the heat pump to the natural gas furnace at an outdoor temperature of **35°F**.

ResStock 2025 Release 1 doesn't run the two at once. Below 35°F the furnace handles the full heating load. The measure documentation gives 25–45°F as the usual range for such systems and cites Lennox's recommendation of about 35°F. The upgrade names also carry the "35F switchover" label.
